claims.statement: HubSpot's authentication overview describes a client secret as a confidential value specific to an app, used to manage OAuth tokens, validate requests from HubSpot and generate a client credentials token, and says a compromised secret can be rotated.

sources.supports: A client secret is a confidential value specific to your app, which is used for managing OAuth tokens, validating requests from HubSpot, and generating a client credentials token.
The X-HubSpot-Signature-v3 header will be an HMAC SHA-256 hash built using the client secret of your app combined with details of the request.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.

openQuestions.question: This candidate is not researched beyond existence: the pages read name the credential but state no literal prefix, alphabet, length or checksum, and no format is recorded or inferred.

The client id is public-facing configuration used beside the secret; whether it is a benign sibling is not researched. The docs show masked UUID-like placeholders for client_id and client_secret, which are not stated to be the format.
